title: Unity of type is explained by unity of descent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Unity of type is explained by unity of descent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The fundamental agreement in structure among organisms of the same class, independent of their habits of life, is explained by their common descent.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: On my theory, unity of type is explained by unity of descent.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “The law of Unity of Type and of the Conditions of Existence embraced by the theory of Natural Selection.”. Scope: organisms within the same class

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independent molecular trees and broad morphology directly test whether unity of type tracks descent. Strong existing coverage and standard comparative methods make the central empirical consequence resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether shared structural plans covary with independently inferred common ancestry more strongly than with present ecology, using morphological and molecular phylogenies. Nested homology matching ancestry supports the claim; repeated ecology-based grouping independent of ancestry opposes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Some morphological characters also inform classifications and can create circularity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.76
data existence: 0.94
discriminating power: 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The explanatory claim has a direct comparative test: fundamental structure should track an independently estimated genealogy rather than way of life. Open trees, sequences, and morphological matrices cover the major classes well enough for that test, and using molecules avoids circularity with a morphology-based taxonomy. A small team can run the comparison with standard phylogenetic methods in weeks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within a class, compare a morphological distance matrix of fundamental structure with a molecular tree and with ecological similarity. Agreement with the molecular tree, and not with habits of life, supports unity of descent; grouping by habit rather than by independent genealogy would refute that explanation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some classes still have sparse morphological matrices or molecule-poor regions of the tree.

Particular characters can be conserved by constraint even when the nested body plan fits descent.
